 THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

These two appeals are filed by the claimant as well as the Insurance Company under 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, (in short MV Act) challenging the judgment and award passed by the VII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes (SCCH-3)/ MACT, Bangalore, in MVC No.2448/2010,
dated 28.09.2012.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience parties herein are referred with original ranks occupied by them before the Tribunal.
3. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that on 16.07.2008, the claimant was traveling in a Meru Cab, bearing registration No.KA-53/6150, to go to Bangalore International Airport.

At that The New India Assurance Co Tld vs Sri Prakash K on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40744210/
4 time, the driver of vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01/AA-5360, drove it in NC:
2023:KHC:41230 a rash and negligent manner and took a 'U' turn on the road median and moved to right side of the road suddenly and stopped in the middle of the road.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co Tld vs Sri Prakash K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a result, the claimant's vehicle came from back side and hit the hind portion of said vehicle.
Due to the said impact, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital for treatment as an inpatient from 16.07.2008 to 02.08.2008.
The claimant was working as a Manager under Intelligroup Asia Private Ltd., and drawing a salary of Rs.1,30,636/- p.m.

Due to the accident,
the claimant suffered both physically and mentally and hence, he filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming a compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents.
4. Initially the prosecution was made as against respondents No.1 to 3 alone.
But, subsequently respondents No.4 and 5 were also added, who were the owner and driver of Meru Cab in which the claimant was traveling.
The respondents No.2 and 3 filed an objection statement disputing the claim and it is asserted that the liability of respondent No.3 is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.
However, the coverage of policy of the offending vehicle has been admitted.
But, it is disputed that the accident is because of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Canter.
But, it is asserted that the accident is because of the actionable negligence of driver of the Meru Cab.
Hence, they have sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

6. After appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, the claim petition came to be allowed in part by the Tribunal by awarding total compensation of Rs.94,550/- by fastening the liability against respondents No.2 and 3 and it is directed that respondent No.3 shall pay the compensation awarded.

7. Being aggrieved by the judgment and award, the claimant has filed MFA No.4422/2013 seeking enhancement, while the Insurance Company i.e., NC: 2023:KHC:41230 respondent No.3 filed MFA No.1871/2013, challenging the liability.

8. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant and the learned counsel for respondent No.3- Insurance Company, who is the appellant-claimant in MFA No.1871/2013.
9.
Perused the records.
10. The learned counsel for the appellant-claimant would contend that the compensation awarded under the head of pain and suffering is on lower side.
He would also assert that the compensation awarded under Medical expenses, Attendant charges, Conveyance, Food and Nutrition and Amenities is also on lower side and sought for enhancement.

The New India Assurance Co Tld vs Sri Prakash K on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40744210/
5 11.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co Tld vs Sri Prakash K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.3- Insurance Company would contend that the entire liability was fastened on respondents No.2 and 3, though the driver of both the vehicles have been prosecuted and NC: 2023:KHC:41230 since there is a contributory negligence, the liability ought to have been fastened to 50% on the vehicle in which the claimant was traveling.

12. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, it is evident from the records that claimant has suffered fracture of 4th metacarpal bone of right hand, lacerated wound of the outer aspect of right thigh, the fracture of 2nd to 8th ribs of right side and fracture of right temporal bone with extra dural haematoma.

Hence, it is evident that the claimant has suffered in all 9 fractures and under the pain and agony, the compensation only to the extent of Rs.50,000/- was awarded by the Tribunal, which is on lower side.
The Tribunal has not considered the gravity of the fractures especially fracture to the left temporal bone with extra dural haematoma.
Hence, compensation awarded under the head of pain and agony to the tune of Rs.50,000/- is on lower side and it needs to be enhanced to Rs.90,000/-.
Further, the Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41230 Rs.10,000/- only under the head of loss of amenities.
But, considering the 9 fractures the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on lower side and as such, under the head of loss of amenities, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/-.
13. The records disclose that, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,500/- under the head of attendant charges and Rs.8,000/- under the head of Conveyance, Food and Nutrition.

It appears to be on lower side and considering the nature and gravity of the injuries, I propose to award Rs.15,000/-
under the head of Attendant charges, Conveyance, Food and Nutrition.
14. Under the head of medical expenses, the claimant has produced documents to show that, he spent Rs.3,24,000/- towards medical expenses.
The Tribunal has considered that the claimant has already reimbursed Rs.3,00,000/- under medical policy and hence, awarded Rs.24,000/- alone.

The learned counsel for the appellant-claimant in this context placed reliance on a decision of the Bombay High Court reported in First Appeal No.1620 of 2012 along with Civil Application No.4005 of 2012 in First Appeal No.1620 of 2012 in the case of Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Mr. Ajit Chandrakant Rakvi and Another, dated 19th March 2019 and argued that the medical expenses were based on premium paid by the claimant and it cannot be deducted.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
16. However, the learned counsel for the respondent on this point has placed reliance on a decision reported in 2013 ACJ 2478 in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Manish Gupta and Another, wherein the Division Bench of this Court has considered this aspect and has observed as under:
The New India Assurance Co Tld vs Sri Prakash K on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40744210/
6 "Quantum-Injury-Principles of assessment- Reimbursement of medical expenses- Mediclaim policy-Medical expenses are classified as pecuniary loss which means the actual amount which is spent by the claimant for treatment-Whether a claimant can claim medical expenses incurred by him for treatment of injuries sustained in accident under both mediclaim policy and - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41230 claim application under Motor Vehicles Act- Held: no; amount received by claimant under mediclaim policy is required to be deducted from total compensation awardable to claimant under the head medical expenses. (1999 ACJ 10 (SC) distinguished: 2000 ACJ 701 (MP) dissented)."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. Hence, in view of the law laid down by the Division Bench of this Court amount received by the claimant under Mediclaim Policy is required to be deducted from the total compensation awarded to the claimant under the head of medical expenses.
18. The Tribunal has rightly deducted Rs.3,00,000/- and awarded Rs.24,000/- which does not call for any interference.
19. The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.

Though the claimant was earning Rs.1,30,636/-, his take home salary is around Rs.96,598/-
which can be rounded to Rs.96,500/-.

In the absence of any other material evidence and considering the number of fractures and head injury including the fracture of temporal bone, the claimant would have been prevented for attending his normal work atleast for two months.
Hence, claimant would be entitled for Rs.1,93,000/- under the head of loss of income during laid up period as he would have encashed the said leave.

21. Since the claimant continued to be in service and since there is no reduction in his rank or salary,
question of considering either disability or loss of future income does not arise at all.

Hence, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under the various heads as under:
1. Pain and agony Rs.90,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.24,000/-
3. Attendant charges, Conveyance, Rs.15,000/-

7

sentences.text:
Food and nutrition 4. Loss of amenities and unhappiness Rs.40,000/-
5. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.1,93,000/-
 Total Rs.3,62,000/-
 - 14 -  NC: 2023:KHC:41230

Hence, the claimant would be entitle for compensation Rs.3,62,000/- as against Rs.94,550/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
22. The contention of the Insurer is regarding contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the Car.

But, the records disclose that, though the driver of the Car was also prosecuted, Ex.P.5 the Sketch of scene of the offence, disclose that the driver of offending Tanker Lorry entered the main road from a cross road and in the process of taking 'U' turn suddenly stopped.
He is required to stop and proceed after observing the traffic.
But, no such evidence is forthcoming.

Further, the claimant is at liberty to claim compensation against any of the tortfeasors and in the instant case the claimant is claiming compensation against the Insurance Company of the offending Tanker Lorry.

Hence,
question of fastening the contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the Car does not arise at all.
Hence, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company in MFA No.1871/2013 does not - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:41230 survive for consideration, while MFA No.4422/2013 needs to be allowed-in-part.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) MFA No.4422/2013 is allowed-in-part.
(ii) The appellant-claimant is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,62,000/- as against Rs.94,550/- awarded by the Tribunal.

(iii) The entire enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(iv) The respondent No.3 - Insurance Company, who is the appellant in MFA No.1871/2013 is liable to pay the entire enhanced compensation with accrued interest thereon.

(vi) The entire enhanced compensation shall be released in favour of claimant.
- 16 -  NC: 2023:KHC:41230  (vii) MFA No.1871/2013 filed by respondent  No.3-Insurance Company stands  dismissed.
(viii) The amount in deposit made by the Insurance Company in MFA No.1871/2013 shall be transmitted to the Tribunal for disbursement.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) MFA No.4422/2013 is allowed-in-part.
(ii) The appellant-claimant is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,62,000/- as against Rs.94,550/- awarded by the Tribunal.
